ai.definition: Space-Based Solar Power (SBSP) is a technology that involves deploying large solar power stations in orbit around the Earth to collect solar energy, which is then transmitted back to Earth's surface via microwaves or lasers.
ai.howItWorks: SBSP systems use large arrays of photovoltaic cells in space to capture unfiltered sunlight. The collected energy is converted into microwaves and beamed towards designated receiving stations on the ground where it is converted back into electricity.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the limitations of traditional solar power by providing a constant, uninterrupted source of clean energy that is not affected by weather or night-time conditions.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves creating large, lightweight solar panels and phased-array antennas capable of transmitting energy over long distances. These components are then integrated into a robust spaceworthy structure designed to withstand the harsh environment of space.
ai.buildProcess: SBSP systems require extensive design and testing phases on Earth before deployment in orbit. The construction involves assembling modules in a controlled environment, followed by rigorous testing for durability and performance under space conditions.
ai.costDrivers: High initial investment due to the complexity and scale of the project; launch costs; maintenance and operational expenses over the system's lifetime; technological development challenges.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is still in the early stages of development with significant technical, economic, and regulatory hurdles to overcome before commercial deployment is feasible.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations governing SBSP. However, international agreements such as the Outer Space Treaty would need to be considered for any space-based operations involving energy transmission.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to satellite stability, energy conversion efficiency, and microwaves safety; economic risks due to high initial investment and operational costs; regulatory challenges in establishing frameworks for space-based power generation.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage given the high development costs and lack of a mature market. Potential profitability would depend on successful demonstration projects and scaling up of technology.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments could include advancements in solar panel efficiency, phased-array antenna technology, and energy storage solutions to address intermittency issues.

glossary.def: Arrays of antennas that can be electronically controlled to direct the beam of microwaves or lasers used for energy transmission.
Electromagnetic waves with frequencies between 300 MHz and 300 GHz, used in this context to transmit solar power from space to Earth.

subsystems.name: Solar array
subsystems.role: collects unfiltered sunlight without night, clouds or atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Power conversion and transmitter
subsystems.role: converts direct current into microwaves and radiates them as a steerable beam.
parts: large phased-array antenna with many thousands of elements

subsystems.name: Beam steering and control
subsystems.role: points the beam at one small spot on the ground and keeps it there.

subsystems.name: Rectenna
subsystems.role: ground antenna that catches the microwaves and rectifies them back into electricity.

subsystems.name: Assembly and orbit infrastructure
subsystems.role: gets the mass to orbit and builds the station there.

buildSteps.title: Design modular units
buildSteps.detail: The station is split into repeatable tiles — array sections and transmitter panels — small enough to launch and join robotically.

buildSteps.title: Make ultra-light components
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film cells and thin antenna panels are produced on rolls, because every kilogram saved cuts launch cost.

buildSteps.title: Launch to orbit
buildSteps.detail: Components are carried to low orbit by reusable launchers, then raised toward geostationary or a suitable high orbit.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Robots and docking tugs connect modules into a structure kilometres wide, with no astronaut assembly assumed.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and point
buildSteps.detail: Arrays unfold and orient to face the Sun while the transmitter faces Earth.

buildSteps.title: Acquire the ground link
buildSteps.detail: A pilot beam from the rectenna tells the array exactly where to aim; phase control forms and holds the microwave beam.

buildSteps.title: Build the rectenna
buildSteps.detail: A receiving field is installed on land or offshore, sized in kilometres to match the beam footprint.

buildSteps.title: Condition and deliver power
buildSteps.detail: Rectified DC is converted and fed into the grid.

buildSteps.title: Operate and dispose
buildSteps.detail: The station is maintained for decades, then deorbited or moved to a graveyard orbit.

prerequisites.why: reusable rockets are flying, but the cost per kilogram is still one to two orders of magnitude above what a power station would need.
kilowatts have been sent tens of metres in ground tests, and a small satellite beamed detectable power to Earth from orbit in 2023, but not at useful scale or efficiency.
cells and structures must be far lighter per watt than today's spacecraft panels.
nothing this large has ever been assembled autonomously in orbit.
the beam must never drift onto aircraft, people or satellites, and must hit a receiver only kilometres wide from geostationary distance.

pathway.milestone: subscale demonstrations such as orbital beaming tests and ground microwave transmission
pathway.unlocks: proof that the individual pieces work.

pathway.milestone: kilowatt-to-megawatt orbital demonstration beaming power to a ground rectenna
pathway.unlocks: real efficiency numbers for a full system.

pathway.milestone: a pilot plant with robotic assembly and a multi-kilometre rectenna
pathway.unlocks: understanding of cost, safety and reliability.

pathway.milestone: gigawatt-scale stations — viable only if launch falls to a small fraction of today's price
pathway.unlocks: firm, near-continuous power exportable to any country with a receiving site.
